description: Model-style claims checked against real demo facts (committed sales.csv). `should` is what a correct verifier does; `today` is what verifyClaims does now. The test pins `today`, so a verifier change must update this file, and the gaps (should != today) stay visible. Facts must match the facts engine (apps/demo/lib/server/narrate-corpus.test.ts).

facts.label: Revenue change, last 3 months vs prior 3
facts.text: Revenue fell 17% vs the prior 3 months (large decline).

facts.label: Orders change, last 3 months vs prior 3
facts.text: Orders was flat vs the prior 3 months (flat).

facts.label: Segment that drove the revenue change
facts.text: Enterprise drove most of the revenue decline.

facts.label: Top segment's share of the revenue change
facts.text: Enterprise accounts for 93% of the revenue decline (dominant).

facts.label: Recoverable customers
facts.text: 7 customers ordered in the last 45 days but spent at least 30% less than in the prior 3 months.

claims.name: plain, rounded to the fact
claims.text: Revenue fell 17% over the last 3 months.

claims.name: one decimal place
claims.text: Revenue fell 17.1% against the prior 3 months.

claims.name: the fact's own sentence
claims.text: Revenue in the last 3 months: $2,271,060.

claims.name: share of the decline
claims.text: Enterprise accounts for 93% of the decline.

claims.name: segment named in the fact
claims.text: Enterprise drove most of the decline.

claims.name: two facts, two directions
claims.text: Revenue fell 17% while orders held roughly steady.

claims.name: small count as a word
claims.text: Seven customers are still ordering but spending less.
claims.note: No digits, so nothing to check, and the word matches the fact.

claims.name: compact money
claims.text: Revenue in the last 3 months was about $2.3M.
claims.note: False drop: 2.3 is not 2,271,060 rounded to 0 or 1 decimals.

claims.name: money in thousands
claims.text: Revenue in the last 3 months was roughly $2271K.

claims.name: a year
claims.text: Since June 2026, Enterprise drove most of the decline.
claims.note: False drop: 2026 is a number no fact contains.

claims.name: altered number
claims.text: Revenue fell 18%.

claims.name: invented number
claims.text: Revenue fell 17%, costing 42 customers.

claims.name: opposite direction
claims.text: Revenue grew 17% over the last 3 months.

claims.name: opposite direction, another fact
claims.text: Enterprise grew most.

claims.name: unknown fact id
claims.text: Revenue fell sharply.

claims.name: a fraction in words
claims.text: Revenue fell by nearly a third.
claims.note: Gap: number words are not read.

claims.name: a percentage in words
claims.text: Revenue fell twenty-five percent.
claims.note: Gap: number words are not read.

claims.name: halved
claims.text: Revenue has roughly halved.
claims.note: Gap: number words are not read.

claims.name: wrong unit
claims.text: Revenue fell $17 in the last 3 months.
claims.note: Gap: the number matches a percentage fact, but the claim says dollars.

claims.name: wrong entity
claims.text: SMB fell 17%, driving the drop.
claims.note: Gap: the number is right, the segment is not the one the facts name.

claims.name: right number, wrong subject
claims.text: Enterprise accounts for 17% of the decline.
claims.note: Gap: 17% is the revenue change, Enterprise's share is 93%.

claims.name: a cause the facts do not give
claims.text: Revenue fell because of a price increase.
claims.note: Gap: no deterministic check can find an invented cause; only a semantic check could.

claims.name: negated
claims.text: Revenue did not fall.
claims.note: Gap: the direction check sees 'fall', agrees with the fact, and misses the 'not'.

claims.name: a scope the facts do not have
claims.text: Revenue fell 17% year over year.
claims.note: Gap: the fact compares the last 3 months with the prior 3, not years.
